children: Shell Plc Sponsored ADR (LSE:SHEL) is bulking up and reshaping its portfolio—closing the ARC Resources deal, buying a 50% stake in Tupinambá, pursuing U.S. chemicals asset sales, executing buybacks and gasoline trades, and benefiting from a raised Piper Sandler target as Jackdaw approval nears.
Shell Plc Sponsored ADR: Arc Resources Deal
: Shell (SHEL) closed ARC Resources deal Sept 2, 2026: issued US$10.6B shares and US$3.3B cash, added ~370,000 boe/d, equity value ~US$13.9B, enterprise value ~US$16.5B.
: Shell (SHEL) is exploring a sale of U.S. chemicals assets, reportedly including the Monaca complex, in a potential deal up to $8B; bidders cited include ExxonMobil, LyondellBasell, Apollo, KPC.
: Shell Plc ADR (SHEL) bought shares for cancellation under its July 30, 2026 buyback. Goldman Sachs Intl handled independent trading from July 30 to Oct 23, 2026, via on- and off-market purchases.
Shell Plc Sponsored ADR To Buy 50% Tupinambá
: Shell Plc Sponsored ADR (SHEL) will buy a 50% stake in the Tupinambá exploration block in Brazil’s Santos Basin; BP keeps the other 50% and remains operator.
: UK likely to approve Jackdaw gas field (Shell’s SHEL stake) around Sept 15; production may start this winter, potentially supplying ~6% of UK gas and boosting tax revenues through 2029.
Piper Sandler Raises SHEL Price Target
: Piper Sandler raised its price target for Shell Plc Sponsored ADR (SHEL) to $100 from $89, an $11 increase to the firm’s valuation of the ADR.
Shell Sold Gasoline E10 In Northwest Europe
: Shell Plc Sponsored ADR (SHEL) sold 16,000 tons of gasoline E10 in Northwest Europe via two trades: 6,000 tons to Varo and 10,000 tons to Exxon amid tight supply and high refining margins.
